🔐 Compliance Data Leak Exposes 291 Crypto Users' Identities

A data leak has linked the real identities of 291 crypto users directly to their wallet activity, stripping away the anonymity they relied on.

Copied support records exposed varying combinations of personal identity, location, and compliance data. Private keys and customer funds were not compromised in the incident.

The breach highlights a persistent vulnerability in crypto: while blockchain transactions can be pseudonymous, KYC and compliance records held by centralized services create a paper trail that, if exposed, can permanently de-anonymize users.

📌 Bitcoin price stalls near $82K as key resistance holds 

🌐 Bitcoin price pulled back after briefly breaking above $82,000 on Sept. 4, as traders took profits following a short squeeze driven by softer Federal Reserve expectations and renewed demand for US spot Bitcoin ETFs. According to data from cryptonews, Bitcoin price traded near $81,150 at the time of writing, having failed to hold an intraday move above the $82,000 psychological level. The pullback left the asset about 1% below its local high but still well above the $80,000 mark reclaimed during the previous session. 

⚠️ The rally accelerated after Bitcoin moved out of a range around $77,000–$79,000. Short sellers were forced to close leveraged positions as the price crossed $80,000, adding automatic buy orders to the market. CoinGlass data cited by market reports showed that the broader crypto market recorded more than $500 million in liquidations during the rally, with short positions accounting for most of the total. Bitcoin shorts reportedly absorbed about $415 million of those losses.

📊 Price action has since slowed near a technically important area. Galaxy Research data shared by analyst Quinten François placed Bitcoin’s 50-week moving average near $81,041, almost level with the current market price. According to François, Bitcoin has not closed a weekly candle above that moving average since November 2025. He said a move through $82,800 would also produce the first higher high of the broader downtrend and bring $90,000 back into consideration.

NSA Launches Sweeping Restructuring Focused on AI, China And Cyber Threats 🚀


The National Security Agency is preparing for its most significant internal overhaul in at least a decade, as the intelligence agency moves to reshape its operations around artificial intelligence, China, cybersecurity and military support.

The restructuring is being driven by NSA Director Gen. Joshua M. Rudd and is expected to reorganize major elements of the agency’s headquarters at Fort Meade, Maryland.

Under the proposed structure, five new mission organizations would be established, focusing on artificial intelligence, China, cybersecurity, combat support and global intelligence. Each would be headed by a newly elevated mission director with broad authority over the organization’s work.

The changes reflect a growing shift in U.S. intelligence priorities. Artificial intelligence has rapidly become a central element of the competition between Washington and Beijing, while cyber operations remain a critical component of both national defense and modern warfare.

The plan would also give the agency a more centralized structure for addressing China, reflecting the country’s expanding importance across U.S. intelligence and national security operations.

One of the more consequential changes could involve leadership. Officials familiar with the plan said some senior positions could potentially be filled by candidates from outside the NSA, a move that could bring new expertise into an agency traditionally dependent on career intelligence personnel.

The proposed restructuring comes as the NSA faces pressure to adapt more quickly to emerging technologies and a changing strategic environment. Rather than organizing primarily around traditional intelligence functions, the new model would place greater emphasis on specific national-security missions.

Implementation is expected to begin this fall, with the agency aiming to have the new structure operating at full capacity by early 2027.

For the NSA, the overhaul represents more than an administrative reorganization. It signals an effort to redesign one of America’s most powerful intelligence institutions around the technologies, adversaries and battlefields that are increasingly defining the next era of national security.
